claim: Prior biomedical SAM studies used only the default SAM without domain retraining, which the authors found crucial
quote: these studies were limited to the default SAM and did not implement retraining for their respective domains, which is crucial according to our findings

claim: Default SAM segments clusters of cells as a single object
quote: SAM segments clusters of cells as a single object

claim: μSAM adds a decoder predicting foreground plus distances to object centers and boundaries, giving automatic instance segmentation (AIS) via post-processing
quote: we add a new decoder to the model that predicts foreground as well as distances to object centers and boundaries

claim: Interactive segmentation is evaluated by adding a corrective positive/negative point pair from prediction errors for seven iterations
quote: This process is repeated seven times (iterations 1–7)

claim: ViT-L gave the best runtime/quality trade-off and was trained for 250,000 iterations on LIVECell
quote: We found that ViT-L provides the best trade-off between runtime and quality

claim: Interactive segmentation with the LIVECell specialist beat all automated methods, whereas the default model reached CellPose only after several correction iterations
quote: whereas it only reaches the performance of CellPose after several correction iterations for the default model

claim: Specialist models improved consistently with more annotations; the default model did not
quote: The specialist models also achieve a consistent improvement when provided with more annotations, which is not the case for the default model.

claim: AIS, available only after fine-tuning, was on par with CellPose on LIVECell
quote: segmentation with AIS, which is only available after fine-tuning, is on par with CellPose

claim: Fine-tuning the image encoder had the biggest impact; fine-tuning the full model was best overall
quote: fine-tuning the image encoder has the biggest impact

claim: Most of the fine-tuning improvement on LIVECell came with only 2%, 4% and 5% of the training data
quote: the majority of improvement is achieved with training data fractions of 2%, 4% and 5%

claim: One model improving across microscopy modalities is not feasible with SAM's architecture, so separate LM and EM generalists were trained
quote: training a single model that consistently improves across different microscopy modalities is not feasible given the current SAM architecture

claim: The LM generalist performed similar to or better than specialists, except AIS on LIVECell
quote: The generalist model overall performs similar or better than the specialist, except for AIS on LIVECell.

claim: LM generalist AIS was on par or better than CellPose except on TissueNet
quote: via AIS performs on par or better than CellPose except for TissueNet

claim: The TissueNet gap is attributed partly to its two channels not mapping well to SAM's RGB input
quote: contains two channels, which do not map well to the RGB inputs of SAM

claim: Comparisons on DeepBacs, PlantSeg (Root) and NeurIPS CellSeg favour μSAM because it trained on their training splits, unlike CellPose cyto2
quote: are heavily biased in our favor

claim: COVID IF, PlantSeg (ovules), Lizard and Mouse Embryo were the LM settings not represented in training
quote: COVID IF, PlantSeg (ovules), Lizard and Mouse Embryo contain image settings not directly represented in training

claim: Mouse Embryo is particularly difficult because of small cell sizes
quote: which represents a particularly difficult problem due to small cell sizes

claim: On Lizard and Mouse Embryo no automated method worked well, but interactive segmentation gave good results, improved by the generalist
quote: but interactive segmentation yields good results and is improved by the generalist

claim: The authors claim LM generalist automatic segmentation is similar to CellPose for most practical settings, not better, while adding interactive segmentation
quote: it provides similar quality for most practical settings, while also enabling interactive segmentation

claim: A generic EM model is harder because EM labels membrane-bound structures unspecifically instead of a specific stain
quote: in EM membrane-bound structures are labeled unspecifically rather than having a specific stain for a cellular component

claim: The EM generalist (MitoLab, MitoEM, PlatyEM) reliably improves only mitochondria, nuclei and other roundish organelles
quote: it reliably improves EM segmentation only for mitochondria, nuclei and other roundish organelles

claim: NucMM (Mouse) nuclei imaged with high-energy X-ray were included as a modality similar to EM
quote: which contains nuclei imaged in high-energy X-ray

claim: MitoNet was overall comparable to AIS and AMG for automatic mitochondrion segmentation, varying by dataset
quote: find that its performance is overall comparable to AIS and AMG, with results varying across datasets

claim: AIS's advantage over AMG is smaller in EM because AMG works better for well-separated objects like mitochondria than densely packed cells
quote: AMG works better for well-separated objects, like mitochondria in EM, compared to densely packed objects, like cells in LM

claim: Even in EM, AIS is preferable in most cases due to lower runtime
quote: AIS is preferable in most cases due to its lower runtime

claim: The EM generalist overall beat default SAM on cilia and microvilli
quote: and find that our EM generalist model overall performs better compared to the default SAM

claim: For ER and neurites the EM generalist gave marginal benefit or harm, because ER morphology differs and it prefers organelles over the surrounding compartment
quote: We find that our EM generalist only provides marginal benefits or is detrimental in these cases, which is due to the different morphology of ER compared to mitochondria

claim: Specialist models trained for ER and neurites clearly improved performance
quote: We train specialist models for both cases, which clearly improve the performance

claim: Interactive point/box segmentation runs on CPU in about 30 ms per object given precomputed embeddings
quote: is feasible on the CPU in around 30 ms per object, given precomputed embeddings

claim: AIS is much faster than AMG
quote: We also see a big speedup of AIS compared to AMG.

claim: The GPU's main advantage is much faster embedding computation and automatic segmentation
quote: The main advantage of a GPU is strongly decreased runtime for embedding computation

claim: ViT-H generally gives no better results than smaller encoders but costs more; ViT-B or ViT-L recommended
quote: Using ViT Huge (ViT-H) does generally not yield better results but incurs a higher computational cost.

claim: ViT-T is much faster and good for simple tasks but severely degraded on others
quote: ViT-T is much faster and yields good results for simple segmentation tasks but has severely degraded quality for others

claim: CellPose takes about 0.3 s per image on GPU and 1.5 s on CPU
quote: It takes circa 0.3 s to segment an image with the GPU and 1.5 s with the CPU.

claim: μSAM embedding + AIS takes 0.2–1.2 s on GPU and 1.5–7.5 s on CPU depending on model size
quote: takes 0.2–1.2 s on the GPU and 1.5–7.5 s on the CPU, depending on the model size

claim: Fine-tuning on only a few images on a CPU is feasible and clearly improves the model
quote: We find that training on only a few images with a CPU is feasible and that it improves the model clearly for a given task.

claim: LoRA training usually took longer because the model needs more iterations to converge
quote: Training with LoRA results in longer training times in most cases because the model needs more iterations to converge.

claim: Fine-tuning on CPU took 5.3 h versus 30 min on GPU
quote: Training on the CPU in this setting took 5.3 h, while training on the GPU took 30 min.

claim: When μSAM models are worse than default SAM, e.g. EM neurites, fine-tuning should start from the default model
quote: for neurite segmentation in EM, it will likely be better to start from a default model

claim: Volumetric automatic segmentation runs AIS or AMG per slice and merges across slices in post-processing
quote: we implement automated segmentation by running AIS or AMG per slice and merging the results across slices in a post-processing step

claim: Interactive volumetric segmentation and tracking project masks to adjacent slices/frames and rerun SAM
quote: by projecting masks to adjacent slices or frames and rerunning SAM with the derived annotations

claim: In the organoid study the LM generalist gave too-big interactive masks (no organoid-like training data), so default SAM gave better interactive results
quote: interactive segmentation with the generalist yields masks that are too big

claim: Annotation with the LM generalist was faster because its automatic segmentation was better
quote: annotation times with the generalist are faster, because it yields a better automatic segmentation

claim: Pretrained SAM vs CellPose: slightly faster annotation but lower quality against consensus
quote: we find slightly faster annotation times, but also decreased annotation quality compared to the consensus

claim: All tool-assisted annotation was much faster than manual annotation (6.7 s per object)
quote: Annotation is much faster than manual in all cases.

claim: After fine-tuning, μSAM models generalized better to the organoid test split while CellPose models deteriorated
quote: the μSAM models improve consistently, whereas the CellPose models deteriorate

claim: The fine-tuned CellPose models were qualitatively observed to find fewer organoids in the test set
quote: models find fewer organoids in the test set

claim: No clearly better tool for organoids: CellPose starts better, matches after fine-tuning, but generalizes worse
quote: CellPose has a better initial segmentation quality, provides similar annotation speed and quality after fine-tuning, but generalizes worse to similar data

claim: For volume-EM nuclei the default ViT-B worked slightly better than the EM generalist, likely due to resolution differences
quote: which worked slightly better than the EM generalist model, likely due to differences in resolution to our training data

claim: Average annotation time per nucleus: ilastik carving 120 s, μSAM default 84 s, μSAM fine-tuned 24 s
quote: ilastik 120

claim: The tracking study used every third frame to make the task more challenging
quote: using every third frame to make the task more challenging

claim: For tracking, the LM generalist had a clear advantage over default SAM, tracking nuclei better
quote: we see a clear advantage of the LM generalist model over the default SAM; it tracks the nuclei better during interactive annotation

claim: Fine-tuning the generalist on a separate time series did not speed up tracking further
quote: Fine-tuning of this model on a separate time series does not speed up tracking further.

claim: Versus TrackMate, μSAM tracking was a bit slower (no automatic tracking) but gave higher-quality annotations
quote: our method is a bit slower, which is because we currently do not automatically track objects, but yields annotations of higher quality

claim: TrackMate took 19 s per track versus 23–38 s for μSAM variants
quote: TrackMate (stardist) 19

claim: Fine-tuning error metric used segmentation accuracy at IoU 50% because mean segmentation accuracy was too stringent for small objects
quote: because we found that mean segmentation accuracy was too stringent for the small objects to meaningfully compare improvements

claim: Because SAM fine-tuning is slow, μSAM offers no human-in-the-loop fine-tuning after each image as CellPose does
quote: so we do not provide ‘human-in-the loop’ fine-tuning as in CellPose

claim: Computational cost prevents an orthogonal-slice 3D approach like CellPose/MitoNet; μSAM goes slice by slice with post-processing
quote: The computational cost also prevents us from building a 3D segmentation approach that operates on orthogonal slices

claim: CellPose and MitoNet were not retrained on μSAM's training data, so no superiority is claimed
quote: we did not retrain them on our model’s training data
